title: Kobayashi-sensei's Love
notes: Episode 584's subtitle file is missing from subs_resolved/ (only 0583 and 0585 exist locally) -- the middle episode, likely covering deeper suspect interrogation and the voice-identification scene, was not available and is not represented here beyond what 583/585 recap. The tail of 0585.txt (from roughly the timestamp of the lunch-bento scene onward) bleeds into an unrelated Kaitou Kid heist subplot ('Kirin's Horn') that is a different case entirely; it was excluded from this file. Unlike the ep011 convention of omitting all recurring detective-cast nodes, Shiratori and Sato are INCLUDED here because they are not incidental furniture in this episode: Sato physically impersonates Kobayashi as a decoy to trap the culprit, and Shiratori's misremembered/miscommunicated backstory with Kobayashi is literally the episode's titular plot thread. Conan, Kogoro, Ran, Megure, Takagi, and the other Detective Boys are omitted per the standard convention since they play no distinct action role beyond banter. The old lower-fidelity case file correctly identified Kodama Ryuusuke as the culprit and the baseball-bat school attack, but its clue description ('a witness mistakes him for a woman due to long hair and arm position') collapses what the transcript shows is a two-layer misdirection: (1) the bellowed threat Kobayashi-sensei heard in a feminine register was actually the victim's voice, not the culprit's -- Sumida presented masculine but the shirt's right-over-left buttoning and the name's ambiguity confirmed her as female to police -- and Kobayashi mistook the body she found for a man's; (2) the fleeing silhouette she took for a woman's chest was actually Kodama's elbow pressed against his old pitching-shoulder injury while running. Neither element is captured by 'long hair and arm position' alone, so the new file separates them into two clues. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Kobayashi heard a feminine-toned bellow ('hand it over or I'll kill you'), but that voice belonged to the masculine-presenting victim Sumida, not the culprit -- she mistook the body she found for a man's, so she assumed a woman had killed him.
The fleeing silhouette Kobayashi described as having 'a full figure' was actually Kodama's elbow pressed against his injured left shoulder while running, not a woman's chest.

The '0' and '9' Kobayashi saw on the truck were really the letters 'O' and 'S' from OSAKA NICO-NICO TRANSPORTATION, distorted by a wall blocking her view -- tracing the truck led to a driver who placed Kodama and Sumida entering the alley together.
